channel.title: Taiwan Daily Insider
channel.description:
Living in Taiwan but drowning in Chinese-language headlines? Taiwan Daily Insider is your daily 10-minute English briefing — sharp, structured, and built for the people actually working and living here.
Every weekday morning, host Eric breaks down what's really moving the needle in Taiwan:
📈 Markets & Finance — TAIEX movements, NTD/USD & NTD/EUR exchange rates, foreign capital flows, and what it all means for your wallet and career.
💻 Tech & Semiconductors — TSMC, AI supply chains, and Taiwan's role at the center of the global chip war — without the jargon overload.
🏛️ Policy & Expat Life — Gold Card updates, labor law changes, visa news, and anything the government is doing that actually affects you.
🌏 Cross-Strait & Geopolitics — The headlines that shape Taiwan's place on the world stage, explained in plain English.
☀️ Daily Taipei Briefing — Weather, what's trending on PTT and Dcard, and a local event worth knowing about.
What makes us different: every episode is powered by a multi-source AI curation engine that scores dozens of articles for relevance to expats before a single word is written — so you get the stories that matter, not just the ones that trended.
New episode every weekday. No fluff, no filler. Just Taiwan, decoded.

item.title: Taiwan Daily Insider - 2026-04-11
item.description: Good morning, good afternoon, or good evening, wherever you are tuning in from! Welcome to Taiwan Daily Insider, your essential guide to navigating the pulse of Taiwan. I’m your host, and today is Saturday, April 11, 2026. Lets dive into the stories making headlines and shaping conversations across the island.We kick things off today with some significant financial news that will undoubtedly catch the eye of every expat and professional here. The New Taiwan Dollar, or NTD, is on an absolutely epic surge! Following a remarkable 3.07% jump earlier this month, the NTD continued its powerful ascent this morning, opening at 30.91 against the US Dollar. Within a mere 15 minutes, it had already surged by over one NTD, briefly touching the 29 NTD mark. This kind of rapid appreciation is something we havent seen in a while, reflecting strong foreign capital inflows and robust export performance.Now, what does this mean for you? If youre earning in NTD, your purchasing power for imported goods and international travel just got a significant boost. For those of you receiving remittances from abroad in US Dollars, you might find your local spending power slightly diminished, but conversely, if youre sending money *out* of Taiwan, your NTD will go further. This strong NTD is often a signal of confidence in Taiwans economic fundamentals, but it also presents challenges for some of Taiwans export-oriented industries. We’ll be keeping a close eye on whether the Central Bank steps in with any measures to stabilize the currency in the coming days.

item.title: Taiwan Daily Insider - 2026-04-14
item.description: Welcome to Taiwan Daily Insider, your essential guide to whats happening on the island. Im your host, and today is April 13, 2026. After a staggering 3.07% surge just two days ago, a move that sent ripples through global currency markets, the NTD opened today at 30.91 against the US Dollar. But that wasnt the end of the story. Within a mere fifteen minutes of trading, we saw an even more aggressive appreciation, with the currency gaining over one full New Taiwan Dollar, flashing past the 29-dollar mark at one point, before settling strongly later in the day around the 30.25 level. A confluence of factors, primarily Taiwans robust export performance, particularly in the high-tech sector, continues to bring in substantial foreign currency. Furthermore, the massive inflow of foreign investment into the Tai-ex, which well discuss shortly, also bolsters demand for the local currency. The Central Banks measured approach to intervention also suggests a comfort with the NTDs appreciation, reflecting strong confidence in Taiwans economic fundamentals. For foreign professionals, expats, and businesses operating here, this continued strength of the NTD has considerable implications. It means your purchasing power for local goods and services is slightly diminished if youre earning in foreign currency, but it also makes imports cheaper. For those remitting funds back home, its a favorable situation. Overall, it signals a very healthy and dynamic economy, but its certainly a trend to keep a close eye on for financial planning.
